1.title: SELECT - all books
1.explain: Retrieves every column of every row in BOOK.

2.title: WHERE + ORDER BY - recent books
2.explain: WHERE filters rows before they are returned; ORDER BY sorts the result by title.
2.sql:
SELECT title, publish_year
FROM BOOK
WHERE publish_year > 2020
ORDER BY title ASC;

3.title: COUNT + GROUP BY - books per category
3.explain: Groups books by category and counts each group.
3.sql:
SELECT c.category_name, COUNT(*) AS total_books
FROM BOOK b
JOIN CATEGORY c ON b.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name;

4.title: HAVING - categories with more than two books
4.explain: HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY (WHERE filters individual rows before grouping).
4.sql:
SELECT c.category_name, COUNT(*) AS total_books
FROM BOOK b
JOIN CATEGORY c ON b.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;

5.title: AVG - average copy price per branch
5.explain: Average price of the physical copies held at each branch.
5.sql:
SELECT br.branch_name, AVG(bc.price) AS average_copy_price
FROM BOOK_COPY bc
JOIN BRANCH br ON bc.branch_id = br.branch_id
GROUP BY br.branch_id, br.branch_name;

6.title: JOIN - books with publishers
6.explain: Matches each book with its publisher through the foreign key publisher_id.

7.title: View - LOAN_DETAILS
7.explain: The view joins LOAN, MEMBER, BOOK, BOOK_COPY and STAFF, so the application reads loans without repeating the joins.

8.title: Subquery - books newer than the average year
8.explain: The inner query returns one value (the average publish year) which the outer WHERE compares against.

9.title: EXISTS - members who have borrowed
9.explain: For each member the inner query checks whether at least one loan exists.

10.title: LEFT JOIN + SUM - fine vs total paid
10.explain: LEFT JOIN keeps fines with no payment; COALESCE turns the NULL sum into 0.
10.sql:
SELECT f.fine_no, f.amount AS fine_amount,
       COALESCE(SUM(p.amount_paid), 0) AS total_paid
FROM FINE f
LEFT JOIN PAYMENT p ON f.fine_no = p.fine_no
GROUP BY f.fine_no, f.amount;

11.title: Derived attribute - member age
11.explain: Age is not stored; it is calculated from date_of_birth whenever it is needed.
11.sql:
SELECT member_id, full_name,
       TIMESTAMPDIFF(YEAR, date_of_birth, CURDATE()) AS age
FROM MEMBER
WHERE date_of_birth IS NOT NULL;

12.title: Available copies with branch and shelf
12.explain: Copies a member could borrow right now, with where to find them.
12.sql:
SELECT b.title, bc.copy_no, br.branch_name, bc.shelf_location
FROM BOOK_COPY bc
JOIN BOOK b ON bc.book_id = b.book_id
JOIN BRANCH br ON bc.branch_id = br.branch_id
WHERE bc.status = 'Available'
ORDER BY b.title;

13.title: Loans handled by each staff member
13.explain: COUNT(l.loan_id) counts only matched loans, so staff with no loans show 0.
13.sql:
SELECT s.full_name, COUNT(l.loan_id) AS loans_handled
FROM STAFF s
LEFT JOIN LOAN l ON s.staff_id = l.staff_id
GROUP BY s.staff_id, s.full_name
ORDER BY loans_handled DESC;

14.title: Reservations with member and book
14.explain: Shows who reserved which title and the reservation status.
14.sql:
SELECT r.reservation_id, m.full_name, b.title,
       r.reserved_on, r.expires_on, r.status
FROM RESERVATION r
JOIN MEMBER m ON r.member_id = m.member_id
JOIN BOOK b ON r.book_id = b.book_id;

15.title: Payments associated with fines
15.explain: One row per payment; a fine without payments still appears with NULL payment columns.
15.sql:
SELECT f.fine_no, f.amount, p.payment_no,
       p.amount_paid, p.payment_date, p.method
FROM FINE f
LEFT JOIN PAYMENT p ON f.fine_no = p.fine_no
ORDER BY f.fine_no, p.payment_date;

16.title: Overdue loans (view OVERDUE_LOANS)
16.explain: Open loans past their due date, with the number of days overdue calculated from CURDATE().
16.sql:
SELECT * FROM OVERDUE_LOANS
ORDER BY days_overdue DESC;

17.title: Availability of every title (view BOOK_AVAILABILITY)
17.explain: SUM(status = 'Available') counts the available copies of each title (a true comparison counts as 1).
17.sql:
SELECT * FROM BOOK_AVAILABILITY
ORDER BY title;

18.title: Members with an outstanding fine balance
18.explain: Uses FINE_SUMMARY (balance = amount - payments) and keeps only members who still owe money.
18.sql:
SELECT member_id, member_name, SUM(balance) AS total_due
FROM FINE_SUMMARY
GROUP BY member_id, member_name
HAVING SUM(balance) > 0;

19.title: Most borrowed titles
19.explain: Counts loans per title and returns the top five.
19.sql:
SELECT b.title, COUNT(*) AS times_borrowed
FROM LOAN l
JOIN BOOK b ON b.book_id = l.book_id
GROUP BY b.book_id, b.title
ORDER BY times_borrowed DESC, b.title
LIMIT 5;

20.title: Books with all their authors (M:N)
20.explain: BOOK and AUTHOR are joined through BOOK_AUTHOR; GROUP_CONCAT lists several authors in one cell.
20.sql:
SELECT b.title,
       GROUP_CONCAT(a.full_name ORDER BY a.full_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS authors
FROM BOOK b
JOIN BOOK_AUTHOR ba ON ba.book_id = b.book_id
JOIN AUTHOR a ON a.author_id = ba.author_id
GROUP BY b.book_id, b.title;

21.title: Members who have never borrowed
21.explain: The opposite of query 9: members for whom no loan row exists.

22.title: Fine collection by payment method
22.explain: How much has been collected through each payment method.
22.sql:
SELECT method, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(amount_paid) AS collected
FROM PAYMENT
GROUP BY method
ORDER BY collected DESC;

23.title: Loan history of a member
23.explain: The member chosen in the form is bound to the ? placeholder, so user input never becomes part of the SQL text.
23.sql:
SELECT loan_id, book_title, issue_date, due_date, return_date, status
FROM LOAN_DETAILS
WHERE member_id = ?
ORDER BY issue_date DESC;

params.name: member_id
params.label: Member
params.sql: SELECT member_id AS id, CONCAT(member_id, ' - ', full_name) AS label FROM MEMBER ORDER BY member_id

24.title: Books in a category published after a year
24.explain: Two placeholders: the category and the earliest publish year.
24.sql:
SELECT b.book_id, b.title, b.publish_year, p.name AS publisher
FROM BOOK b
LEFT JOIN PUBLISHER p ON p.publisher_id = b.publisher_id
WHERE b.category_id = ? AND b.publish_year >= ?
ORDER BY b.publish_year;

params.name: category_id
params.label: Category
params.sql: SELECT category_id AS id, category_name AS label FROM CATEGORY ORDER BY category_name

25.title: Loans issued between two dates
25.explain: Loans whose issue date falls inside the chosen range (both ends included).
25.sql:
SELECT loan_id, member_name, book_title, issue_date, status
FROM LOAN_DETAILS
WHERE issue_date BETWEEN ? AND ?
ORDER BY issue_date;

overdue.title: Overdue loans
overdue.about: Members to contact today, most overdue first, with the fine due if the book came back today.
overdue.sql:
SELECT o.loan_id AS loan, o.member_name AS member, o.phone, o.book_title AS book,
       o.due_date, o.days_overdue, o.days_overdue * ? AS fine_if_returned_today
FROM OVERDUE_LOANS o
ORDER BY o.days_overdue DESC

branches.title: Stock by branch
branches.about: How many copies each branch holds, how many are on the shelf, and their total value.
branches.sql:
SELECT br.branch_name AS branch,
       COUNT(bc.copy_no) AS copies,
       SUM(bc.status = 'Available') AS available,
       SUM(bc.status = 'Borrowed') AS borrowed,
       SUM(bc.status IN ('Reserved', 'Maintenance')) AS reserved_or_maintenance,
       COALESCE(SUM(bc.price), 0) AS stock_value_rs
FROM BRANCH br
LEFT JOIN BOOK_COPY bc ON bc.branch_id = br.branch_id
GROUP BY br.branch_id, br.branch_name
ORDER BY br.branch_name

categories.title: Usage by category
categories.about: Titles, copies and total loans per category: which parts of the collection are used most.
categories.sql:
SELECT c.category_name AS category,
       COUNT(DISTINCT b.book_id) AS titles,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(bc.book_id, '-', bc.copy_no)) AS copies,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.loan_id) AS times_borrowed
FROM CATEGORY c
LEFT JOIN BOOK b       ON b.category_id = c.category_id
LEFT JOIN BOOK_COPY bc ON bc.book_id = b.book_id
LEFT JOIN LOAN l       ON l.book_id = b.book_id
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name
ORDER BY times_borrowed DESC, category

members.title: Member activity
members.about: Every member with their total loans, books held now against the plan limit, and fines owed.
members.sql:
SELECT s.member_id, s.full_name AS member, s.status, s.plan_name AS plan,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM LOAN l WHERE l.member_id = s.member_id) AS total_loans,
       CONCAT(s.open_loans, ' / ', s.max_books) AS holding_vs_limit,
       s.outstanding_fines AS fines_due_rs
FROM MEMBER_SUMMARY s
ORDER BY total_loans DESC, member

fines.title: Fine collection
fines.about: Money collected by payment method. Outstanding balances are in the summary above.
fines.sql:
SELECT method, COUNT(*) AS payments, SUM(amount_paid) AS collected_rs
FROM PAYMENT
GROUP BY method
ORDER BY collected_rs DESC

monthly.title: Loans per month
monthly.about: Circulation trend: loans issued and returned in each month.
monthly.sql:
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(issue_date, '%Y-%m') AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS loans_issued,
       SUM(return_date IS NOT NULL) AS returned_so_far
FROM LOAN
GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(issue_date, '%Y-%m')
ORDER BY month DESC

phone.label: Phone
phone.pattern_msg: Phone may contain only digits, spaces and hyphens (e.g. 0416-2201000).

branch_id.label: Branch
branch_id.sql: SELECT branch_id AS id, branch_name AS label FROM BRANCH ORDER BY branch_name
